Here is the summary:

The main equipment failure was **Turbine T-4**, taken offline on 14 March 2025 after its **bearing seal corroded through**, allowing seawater into the nacelle; the root cause was traced to corrosion of the bearing seal housing. This was the only failure in the pilot that caused a multi-week outage.

The pilot delivered **18.7 GWh** to the grid over 24 months, which was 6% below the 19.9 GWh forecast.

The project finished at **EUR 41.25 million against an approved budget of EUR 36.7 million**, an overrun of EUR 4.55 million (12.4%), driven mainly by the T-4 repair campaign.

The independent fish-monitoring programme found **no statistically significant change in fish migration counts** before and after installation (p = 0.41).

Lead engineer Dr. Ines Marchetti recommended **replacing the titanium fastener set with duplex stainless steel** on all remaining nacelles, a change the steering group accepted in principle.

The steering group **approved Phase 2 for Q3 2026**, contingent on a completed bearing seal redesign and a successful dry-dock endurance test.
